subject: Post-call: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification — hardware & offline ops next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@legacybank.com>, security@legacybank.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification — hardware & offline ops next steps

Tom / Legacy team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the items we discussed so we can keep momentum: 

1) Deployment modes considered: hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem, air-gapped). Your security team confirmed Private VPC / on-prem air-gap is the preferred path for the PII workloads on the payments ledger.

2) Open technical questions from our side to validate sizing and plan:
   - Expected QPS and steady-state tokens/sec per workload (approx).
   - Acceptable single-node and cluster maintenance windows for kernel/OS updates.
   - Process for applying software updates in an air-gapped environment (USB package vs sealed image).
   - Onsite ops staffing model (do you have an infra team to handle reboots, rack swaps?) and escalation contacts.
   - KMS/HSM integration constraints and any approved vendors.

3) Next steps we proposed:
   - You to share infra inventory / rack constraints and any current GPU types.
   - Redwood to provide a preliminary hardware recommendation and offline ops checklist.
   - Schedule a technical deep-dive with your offline ops and infra leads (suggest 60–90m).

Can you please send the infra inventory (CPU, RAM, GPU, storage, networking) and the security requirements doc you mentioned? I’ll loop in our infra lead (Rishi) to prepare the checklist and a recommended HW starting point.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf (preliminary checklist we discussed)

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

---
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference for production LLMs

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@legacybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legacy Bank - Security Team <security@legacybank.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification — hardware & offline ops next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and attachments from our side: 

- Attached: LB-Infra-Specs.pdf (current rack inventory) and Security-Requirements.xlsx (approved controls).
- Expected load: initial pilot ~50 concurrent requests, peak testing up to 400 qps with short bursts. Average prompt length ~600 tokens; embedding workloads separate and low QPS.
- Air-gap model: we do not allow outbound internet from the inference racks. Updates are performed via signed update package on removable media; remote access only via jump-box in a separate management VLAN when explicitly enabled for maintenance windows.
- Onsite ops: we have an infra on-call (2 people) per shift; they can perform reboots and physical swaps but we will need step-by-step runbooks for any advanced recovery.
- KMS: Approved vendors listed in the spreadsheet; we have an HSM appliance (nShield) we prefer for key wrapping.
- Procurement: approval process complete; procurement timeline ~6–8 weeks after SOW and HW quote.

We’d like Redwood to propose:
  * Minimum HW spec for pilot (nodes / GPUs / storage),
  * Upgrade path for higher throughput, and
  * Recommended offline update process that matches our signed-package flow.

Also please propose 2 times for the deep-dive — prefer Wed/Thu next week 10–12 PT.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Payments Platform
Legacy Bank
tom.ellis@legacybank.com | (617) 555-3344

On the attachments: files referenced above.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@legacybank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification — hardware & offline ops next steps

Tom — appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments. Quick reply with proposed plan and agenda for the deep-dive: 

Proposed pilot HW (preliminary; we’ll size after the deep-dive):
- 2 x rack nodes, each with 4 x A100 80GB (NVMe local storage 6TB), 1 x 25GbE uplink per node. This config supports low-latency generation for the pilot and gives headroom for parallel requests.
- If you prefer a smaller power footprint we can offer quantized model variants that run on lower-memory GPUs; we’ll discuss trade-offs in the tech call.

Upgrade path: additional nodes + model sharding/batching; we’ll provide throughput estimates for each step.

Offline update proposal (summary):
- Redwood builds signed update image for the inference runtime and model bundles.
- We deliver an encrypted, signed package via SFTP to a secure staging host (or via physical media per your policy). Your on-site infra can validate signatures against your HSM/KMS.
- Rishi will prepare a detailed runbook that maps to your signed-package process and a fallback rollback procedure.

Proposed tech deep-dive agenda (60–90m):
1) Introductions & goals (5m)
2) Walk through current infra inventory (you) + constraints (10m)
3) Redwood recommended HW and sizing rationale (15m)
4) Offline update process + signature validation and HSM integration (20m)
5) Ops runbook and DR scenarios (15m)
6) Q&A and next steps / SOW timing (15m)

We can do Wed 29 Sep 10:00 PT or Thu 30 Sep 11:00 PT — please confirm a slot and we’ll send a calendar invite and a preliminary slide deck.

Next actions for you: share any VM images / OS versions you require, and confirm the on-site contact for the infra runbook.

I’ve attached the redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf we mentioned; Rishi and Monica will own the technical materials.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Subject: Internal: Legacy Bank on-prem follow-up prep

Quick internal note — I’ll take point on the runbook and offline update flow. Actions: 
- I will draft the signed-package procedure mapping to Legacy’s Security-Requirements.xlsx and validate HSM integration with our ops tools.
- Monica: can you coordinate a short checklist for the infra inventory fields we need (OS kernel, BIOS versions, IP topology, serial numbers)?
- Jonas: please stand by for a possible join on the deep-dive; we may need your input on the NVMe/IOPS expectations.

I’ll have a draft runbook and preliminary sizing notes by EOD Mon (27 Sep).

Thanks — Rishi
